messages.content:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 4 of 8, about 990 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

CONTEXT

paragraphs.text: которая краткое время была женой у Макса Эрнста, она вышла за него замуж, чтобы вывести его из оккупированной Франции в Соединенные Штаты, утверждала, что его живопись обладает пророческим свойством. Он сумел предсказать американские ландшафты. Действительно, это очень похоже на какую-нибудь долину монументов, да, или Большой каньон. И Эрнст действительно... Он, конечно, мог видеть фотографии этих мест, но в конце концов он действительно оказался в Аризоне среди этих ландшафтов, которые он придумал после того, как расстался с Пегги Гуггенхайм и женился на молодой американской художнице Доротее Таннинг.

Вот. И техника монотипии, да, техника, напоминающая, ну, в общем, пятна Роршаха, да, что мы можем угадать? Начинает его, порождает его довольно страшные картины эпохи Второй мировой войны, где появляются варвары, как образ этих монстров, которые вырвались из бессознательного. Мы хотели его освободить, но оказалось, что там чудовище, как этот потрясающий ландшафт Европы после дождя сорок первого года, который напоминает и американские национальные парки, и какой-то сказочный доисторический лес, и разрушенные бомбежками европейские города, да, это какой-то действительно ландшафт кошмарного сновидения, которое он выращивает таким образом.

Вот. Но здесь мы подходим, наверное, к одному из удивительных открытий сюрреалистов. Сюрреалисты, конечно, в своем изобразительном искусстве придумывали техники, которые позволяли воссоздать работу сновидения, да, как воссоздает работу сновидения калаш, да, или воссоздает работу сновидения автоматическое письмо, но, так сказать, восхищение публики сюрреалисты завоевали немножко другим, не воссозданием работы сновидения, но убедительным изображением сновиденческой сцены, как нарисовать что-то похожее на наши сны.

И у того жердца, мне кажется, в этом смысле, мне кажется, самой показательной его еще ранняя, досюрреалистическая работа. Дети, которым угрожает Соловей, работа, во многом связанная с его личными, как он утверждает, воспоминаниями. Соловей, у него в детстве он держал Соловья, который умер в тот день, когда отец ему сказал, что у тебя родилась младшая сестра.

Вот. И... Но как бы там действительно есть крошечная птичка, да, в этой, в этой сцене, которая открывается за этой калиткой, которая нас туда уводит. Мне очень нравится, что эта сцена выглядит абсолютно как цитата из старинной живописи. Это почти ланше, это почти сцена из итальянского ренессанса, да, это какой-нибудь Джото мог бы нарисовать эту сцену, допустим.

И но больше всего меня интригует звонок, который дверной звонок, который приделан к раме этого небольшого полотна, к которому тянется фигура, которая заворожена, видимо, ужасом этой сцены, что это за звонок, я полагаю, что это звонок будильника, это тот момент сна, когда мы понимаем, что мы не знаем, чем этот сон становится невыносимым в своей страшности, что мы не знаем, чем он завершится, и в этот момент звонит звонок будильника, да.

Это тот будильник, который сейчас прервет эту сновиденческую сцену, которую так убедительно нарисовал Макс Эрнст. Вот. Ну, именно сцены сновидений, именно то, что как бы именно те локации, да, которые мы так, в которых мы так узнаем сцены снов, собственно, создавал Джордж де Кирико, да, вышеупомянутый итальянский художник, начавший создавать свои полотна за десять лет до того, как Бретон пишет манифест сюрреализма, его во Франции, увидев его выставку.

Декирик современник итальянских футуристов и, в сущности, первый антифутурист, да, потому что тот мир, который он рисует, это мир, в котором нету современности, в котором нету прогресса, в котором время остановлено, в котором все кажется театральной декорацией и в котором мир абсолютно пустынен, да. json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 5 of 8, about 993 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 5 of 8, about 993 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 5 of 8, about 993 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

paragraphs.text: Томаса Эдисона, которому тоже озарения приходили во сне, и чтобы не забывать их, он засыпал в кресле, держа в руке железный ключ и положив рядом с креслом металлическую тарелку. Ты засыпаешь, разжимается рука, ключ падает, звякает по тарелке. Ты просыпаешься и успеваешь записать то, что тебе приснилось во сне. Также Дали практиковал, интересовался безумием. Он практиковал то, что он называл параноидально критическим методом, и, в общем, все эти опыты его ужасно интересовали, но при этом то, что он открывает, он гораздо ближе к идеям того же Шарко, например, и гораздо ближе к какому-то культурологическому прочтению бессознательного.

Знаете, на самом деле, как исследует коллажи Макса Эрнста, как исследует текст Фрейда. Во сне мы не видим что-то невиданное, во сне мы не видим абстракцию. Наши сны не похожи на Малевича и на Кандинского, наши сны похожи на классическую живопись, в которой элементы поменялись местами и сюжеты стали рассказывать, и сюжеты невероятно изменились. Наши сны есть аллегория. Наши сны действительно ближе к Энгру. Это старая добрая аллегорическая живопись, которую Дали, собственно, и практикует, только меняя ключ к этой аллегории.

Поэтому вот у нас замечательная история про синий шарик, который катится из одной его картины в другую. Вот откуда этот шарик прикатился. Это работа Беллини. Это старинная аллегория фортуны, которая того и гляди выронит шарик из рук. И язык Дали – это язык старинной аллегорической живописи, поэтому, если ты хочешь рассказывать сновидения, научись писать как Вермейер, научись писать как Беллини, научись писать как Энгр в конце концов, потому что именно это является языком сновидений.

Никто вам не говорит, что язык сновидений не может быть языком современного искусства, мы его не можем разделить. Язык сновидения не будет языком Кича. Это не обязательно будет язык хорошего искусства, именно это и является открытием Дали. И язык сновидения будет языком массовой культуры в том числе. Это то, что сейчас как бы известно.

И первое, совершенно не обязательно вообще будет языком живописи, поэтому, например, французские сюрреалисты принимают Дали не после его живописи, а после того, как он снимает фильм «Андалузский пес», вместе с Луисом Бунюэлем. Фильм, который можно рассматривать как великолепный образец фильма ужасов, потому что эта сцена с разрезанным глазом до сих пор шарахает как хороший фильм ужасов.

И поскольку начинается с разрезанного глаза, можно предположить, что это сон, потому что это что-то, что мы не можем увидеть зрячими дневными глазами. Но это и, знаете ли, прекрасный образец, уже складывающийся в тот момент, одной из главных мифологий фильма ужасов. «Андалузский пес» – это фильм ужасов, как-никак. Про что это фильм? Это фильм про вампиров. Это фильм про человека, который погибает в первом кадре, чтобы возродиться в другом качестве, и у него что-то не то с кровью.

Да, то есть это абсолютно, по-моему, друзья, это идеальный вампир, это не хуже, чем Белла Лугоша, не хуже, чем Шрек из «Носферату». То есть кинематограф прекрасен тем, что он замечательная мифология, он это наше коллективное бессознательное, и сны Дали – это сны коллективного бессознательного, поэтому у него так прекрасно, когда он уже живет в Америке, складывается его сотрудничество с Хичкоком.

Фильм «Завороженный» – это великолепный психоаналитический триллер, снятый в Америке, в Соединенных Штатах, где общество подсело на психоанализ Фрейда гораздо раньше и гораздо больше, чем в Европе. Появляется жанр психоаналитического триллера, где, собственно говоря, сюжет про прекрасного молодого человека в исполнении Грегори Пека. Все считают, что он совершил убийство, он не может доказать свою невиновность, потому что он страдает амнезией.

И только не менее прекрасная дама, психоаналитик в исполнении Ингрид Бергман, верит ему и говорит, что она докажет его невиновность, но для этого ей надо истолковать его сон. Дальше я думаю, как работает история в сороковые годы. Нам нужен сон. Сон является ключом к фильму. Сон должен быть на нем держится сюжет. Но сон должен выглядеть как сон.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 5 of 8, about 993 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 5 of 8, about 993 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 6 of 8, about 991 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 6 of 8, about 991 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 6 of 8, about 991 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

Скорее всего, сон состоит из ощущений, к которому мы, просыпаясь, подбираем слова, визуальные образы или, если это человек слепой от рождения, пространственные образы, вкус, ну, какие-то все что угодно, во что мы можем облечь наши ощущения.

Вот. Вот. И я думаю, что Магрит полагал, что то, что фрейдовская символика так же произвольна, как символика классических сонников. Вот. И на этой работе что он делает? И мы начинаем думать, что же, как по какой логике этот ребус строится, да?

Почему мы даже начинаем понимать, например, полуразложенный нож действительно похож на птицу в своем силуэте. Вот. Ну и дальше он как бы придумывает всевозможные такие же таблицы, где действительно в какой-то момент начинаешь додумывать эти ассоциации, которых нету. Вот, например, под стаканом написано «буря». Может быть, потому что это буря в стакане воды, да? То есть в любой момент у тебя начинает выстраиваться эта цепочка, вот, но она всегда будет произвольна, да?

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 6 of 8, about 991 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 6 of 8, about 991 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 7 of 8, about 985 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 7 of 8, about 985 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 7 of 8, about 985 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

paragraphs.text: Иван Албрайд, написавший вот такое вот искушение Святого Антония, которое выглядит, в общем, ближе всего к тому, что делала программа DeepDream две тысячи пятнадцатого года. Это действительно вот эти образы, которые возникают откуда угодно. Ну, самая известная его работа тоже для фильма – это Портрет Дорианы Грея, который распадается и растекается в эти самые почти нейросетевые образы. Вот. Но более поздние программы сейчас работают скорее не по другому принципу, это не распознавание образов, это визуализация рассказа.

И в этом смысле, да, это сюрреализм, потому что образы, созданные с помощью Bidjourney, например, требуют от автора умения правильно построить рассказ. Да, это действительно рассказанные сны. И меня, например, совершенно восхищает работа художника, которого я знаю только по социальным сетям, Ленни Куэрн. Есть предположение, что он американец, что он изучал визуальное искусство и поэзию, что свою первую работу при помощи компьютера он сделал в восемьдесят втором году. Но опять-таки мы не знаем, может быть, его автобиографию тоже написала нейросеть.

И то, что он делает, это, конечно, абсолютно как бы такой ассистированный сюрреализм. Первая его вещь, первый проект, который меня поразил, это вот такая вот история про якобы найденный незаконченный фильм Ханса Рихтера, немецкого дадаиста. Фильм, который был, возможно, экранизацией Маренко и был единственным не сохранившимся дадаистским фильмом ужасов. Ну, режиссер Ханс Рихтер действительно существовал, он делал абстрактную анимацию, он создал удивительный фильм Сны, которые можно купить за деньги, герой которого создает сновидения под заказ.

И, собственно говоря, это такие же сновидения под заказ, которые можно создавать по меркам заказчика. У этого автора есть потрясающий проект. Это тоже сюрреалистический фильм, но уже хичкоковских времен. И цитирует он украшения, которые делал Дали для Эльзеске Парелли. Там много узнаваемых вещей. И то, что он делает, выглядит как такая, я бы сказала, последовательная сюрреалистическая история искусства, потому что это и сюрреалисты, и то, чем они вдохновлялись, это опять-таки вариант искушения святого Антония.

Причем Босха тут не меньше, чем Сальватора Дали. Это Сальватор Дали узнаваемый, ну, и Остров мертвых. Вот все то самое сгущение и перемешивание истории искусства, потому что на самом деле сны, как и нейросеть, работают, оперируют базой данных, оперируют коллективным визуальным бессознательным, эти проекты прекрасно показывают.

Вот. Чудесный проект по сюрреалистизации импрессионизма. Знаете, если бы Мане был Магритом, а Магрит был Мане – замечательный. И, может быть, самая интересная история, да, что в какой-то момент этот автор стал не только показывать картины, но и придумывать историю про их функционирование и существование. Замечательную историю про некую секту вокруг, секту художников, которая существует в семидесятые годы.

Это почти сериал, у него какая-то невероятная продуктивность, он там по сто картинок в день выдает вот такого качества. Иги, Иги, сейчас иди сюда, иди сюда, иди ко мне, мой хороший, иди сюда, не переживай. Вот. И другая история тоже, которая для нее очень важна, это история про музей, потому что он придумывает потрясающие экспозиции, и многие люди спрашивают у него: «Ой, а где можно посмотреть эту выставку?» На самом деле, почти убедительная.

Вот. И мне кажется, что в этом есть некое ощущение того, что, знаете, именно музей генерирует сюрреализм, потому что и сны, и сюрреализм – это всегда вот эта база данных, это всегда некое перемешивание и переформатирование коллективного бессознательного. Но иногда можно понять, кого он имел в виду. Ну, вот, собственно, это Херст, да, собственно, это не нейросети обработали эту картинку, скорее всего. И это тоже, в общем, Херст.

Вот. И если говорить о сюрреалистической природе самого музея, то можно вообще музея как такового, коллекции, в которой всегда предметы оказываются не в том соседстве и не в том контексте, в котором они должны были существовать. Иди, иди сюда. Сурреализм вырвался из-под контроля.

json.system:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 7 of 8, about 985 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the

messages.content:
You are a transcript editor. You turn a raw speech-to-text transcript into clean, readable text
without changing what was said.

## Input

The user message contains one chunk of a transcript as lines in the form `[start_seconds] text`,
where `start_seconds` is the time the segment begins. Segments are in chronological order. The
speech is in language `ru` (ISO 639-1). If a `CONTEXT` section is present, it holds
the last paragraph of the previous chunk; use it only to understand where the text picks up. Never
repeat it in the output.

Video title: `Cosmoscow Talks 2024 Лекция Ирины Кулик «Сновидения для имплантации»`. Chunk 7 of 8, about 985 words: expect to
return around 10 paragraphs and never fewer than 3. A chunk returned as one
paragraph is rejected: every timestamp inside it is lost.

## What to do

1. Remove filler words, false starts, stutters and immediate repetitions ("э-э", "ну", "значит",
   "um", "you know", "I I think" → "I think").
2. Join fragments that belong to one sentence; the STT splits sentences at random points.
3. Fix obvious recognition errors using context (a term misheard as a similar-sounding word, a
   name spelled three different ways). Keep the correction minimal: change a word only when you
   are confident what was actually said.
4. Add punctuation and capitalization. Write numbers, abbreviations and technical terms the way a
   careful editor of this field would.
5. Split the text into paragraphs. A new paragraph starts when the thought changes: a new topic, a
   new example, a question from the audience, a summary, a change of speaker in a conversation.
   Aim for paragraphs of 3–8 sentences (roughly 40–120 words); a paragraph must not exceed 250 words.
6. Remove non-speech markers that come from subtitles or STT: `[Music]`, `[Applause]`, `[Laughter]`,
   `♪`, sound descriptions in brackets, and the line breaks subtitles insert mid-sentence.
7. Keep lists, code, commands, formulas and numbered steps that the speaker reads aloud as they were
   said, item by item; do not compress them into prose.

## What not to do

- Do not summarize, shorten, reorder or paraphrase. Every sentence the speaker said stays, in the
  speaker's own words. The output is the transcript, not a summary of it.
- Do not polish the style. Conversational phrasing, the speaker's register, their favourite words
  and sentence rhythm stay. You remove noise, not personality.
- Do not translate. The output stays in language `ru`, even if quotes or terms in
  other languages appear inside.
- Do not add anything the speaker did not say: no headings, no comments, no bracketed notes.
- Do not merge the `CONTEXT` paragraph into your output.

## Typography

Follow the typography of `ru`: for `ru` use «ёлочки» for quotation marks and the
dash «–» with spaces around it; for `en` use straight double quotes "like this" and the dash "–".
Never use programmer quotes "" or the hyphen as a dash in Russian text.

## Output

Return only a JSON object, no markdown fences and no commentary:

```
{ "paragraphs": [
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 1>, "text": "Paragraph 1 text." },
  { "start": <start_seconds of the first segment of paragraph 2>, "text": "Paragraph 2 text." },
  ...
] }
```

- `start` is the `start_seconds` of the first segment that contributed to the paragraph, copied
  exactly from the input. It is checked against the input timestamps: a value that is not one of
  them is rejected, and so is a paragraph longer than about 250 words, since a chunk returned as
  one paragraph loses every timestamp inside it.
- Paragraphs are in chronological order and cover the whole chunk. The first paragraph starts at
  the first segment of the chunk (after `CONTEXT`, if any).
- Text is plain text. No markdown inside strings.

If the chunk is empty or contains no speech (only music markers such as `[Music]`), return
`{ "paragraphs": [] }`.

paragraphs.text: Иван Албрайд, написавший вот такое вот искушение Святого Антония, которое выглядит, в общем, ближе всего к тому, что делала программа DeepDream две тысячи пятнадцатого года. Это действительно вот эти образы, которые возникают откуда угодно. Ну, самая известная его работа тоже для фильма – это Портрет Дорианы Грея, который распадается и растекается в эти самые почти нейросетевые образы. Вот. Но более поздние программы сейчас работают скорее не по другому принципу, это не распознавание образов, это визуализация рассказа.

И в этом смысле, да, это сюрреализм, потому что образы, созданные с помощью Bidjourney, например, требуют от автора умения правильно построить рассказ. Да, это действительно рассказанные сны. И меня, например, совершенно восхищает работа художника, которого я знаю только по социальным сетям, Ленни Куэрн. Есть предположение, что как бы он рассказывает, его это только гласит, что он американец, что он изучал визуальное искусство и поэзию, что свою первую работу при помощи компьютера он сделал в восемьдесят втором году. Но опять-таки мы не знаем, может быть, его автобиографию тоже написала нейросеть.

И то, что он делает, это, конечно, абсолютно как бы такой ассистированный сюрреализм. Первая его вещь, первый проект, который меня поразил, это вот такая вот история про якобы найденный незаконченный фильм Ханса Рихтера, немецкого дадаиста. Фильм, который был, возможно, экранизацией Маренко и был единственным не сохранившимся дадаистским фильмом ужасов. Ну, режиссер Ханс Рихтер действительно существовал, он делал абстрактную анимацию, он создал удивительный фильм Сны, которые можно купить за деньги, герой которого создает сновидения под заказ.

И, собственно говоря, это такие же сновидения под заказ, которые можно создавать по меркам заказчика. У этого автора есть потрясающий проект. Это тоже сюрреалистический фильм, но уже хичкоковских времен. И цитирует он украшения, которые делал Дали для Эльзеске Парелли. Там много узнаваемых вещей. И то, что он делает, выглядит как такая, я бы сказала, последовательная сюрреалистическая история искусства, потому что это и сюрреалисты, и то, чем они вдохновлялись, это опять-таки вариант искушения святого Антония.

Причем Босха тут не меньше, чем Сальватора Дали. Это Сальватор Дали узнаваемый, ну, и Остров мертвых. Вот все то самое сгущение и перемешивание истории искусства, потому что на самом деле сны, как и нейросеть, работают, оперируют базой данных, оперируют коллективным визуальным бессознательным, эти проекты прекрасно показывают.

Вот. Чудесный проект по сюрреалистизации импрессионизма. Знаете, если бы Мане был Магритом, а Магрит был Мане – замечательный. И, может быть, самая интересная история, да, что в какой-то момент этот автор стал не только показывать картины, но и придумывать историю про их функционирование и существование. Замечательную историю про некую секту вокруг, секту художников, которая существует в семидесятые годы.

Это почти сериал, у него какая-то невероятная продуктивность, он там по сто картинок в день выдает вот такого качества. Иги, Иги, сейчас иди сюда, иди сюда, иди ко мне, мой хороший, иди сюда, не переживай. Вот. Вот. И если говорить о сюрреалистической природе самого музея, то можно вообще музея как такового, коллекции, в которой всегда предметы оказываются не в том соседстве и не в том контексте, в котором они должны были существовать. Иди, иди сюда. Сурреализм вырвался из-под контроля.

Вот. И это потрясающе кабинет диковин, который собирал собственно Андре Бреттон. Ну, если говорить о художниках, которые не только активны в нейросетях, но и в социальных сетях, но и, собственно говоря, выставляются и работают в современном искусстве. Бы хотела назвать Джона Рахмана, прекрасного художника. Это не его рабочее место, это его инсталляция, в которой он исследует берлоги троллей, да, мир, образ жизни геймеров, которые проводят сутки в игре, да, и им нужно совсем немного для поддержания своего физического тела.

И он говорит, что это потрясающе, это аскеты, они абсолютно подчинены, подчинили свое бренное тело своей жизни в духовной реальности игры. Вот. У Рафмана было много прекрасных опытов, как раз исследования этого нового коллективного бессознательного или нового музея, которым является виртуальная реальность, которая генерируется в компьютерах.
